To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the complement control protein domains 7 and/or 8 of C1qR/C4BP α-chain interacts with the outer membrane protein LigA and LigA of the pathogenic leptospires L. interrogans and L. borgpetersenii serogroup Icterohaemorrhagiae.

the interaction between C4B-Binding Protein and outer membrane proteins LigA and LigA is sensitive to 1) ionic strength, 2) inhibited by heparan sulfate and 3) mediated through the bacterial Immunoglobulin-like (BIG) domains 7-8 of both LigA & LigB.
C4BP binds to the outer membrane proteins LigA and LigA of L. interrogans through the CCP7 and CCP8 of its α-chain and that this interaction is inhibited by heparan sulfate proteoglycans.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the molecular mechanisms of the interaction of C4BP with Lig proteins and how this interaction may contribute to the evasion of pathogenic leptospires from complement activation and killing.
the identification and fine mapping of the binding domains between the pathogenic leptospires and the complement inhibitor C4BP, which may be important to the pathogenesis of leptospirosis.
the identification of a novel mechanism used by pathogenic leptospires to evade complement attack and may be used to develop new diagnostic and/or therapeutic tools against leptospirosis.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the interaction of Lig proteins with C4BP and FH is mediated through CCPs 7 and 9 and the Big domains of LigA and LigA and Lig proteins, respectively.
LigA and Lig B proteins from pathogenic leptospires interact with C4BP through the CCPs 7 and 9, and heparin through the Big 7-8 domains of LigA and LigA7-8, LigB7-10, LigB9-8, LigA7-10 and LigB7.
C4BP and FH are the two most important complement regulators that interact with Lig proteins, thus allowing the pathogen to escape from complement-mediated killing.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the pathogenic leptospires L. interrogans and L. kirschneri have evolved a mechanism that allows them to escape complement-mediated lysis by binding to host C4BP and by mimicking heparin, a natural inhibitor of the complement system.
the interaction between LigA and LigA is a very important tool for the study of the interaction between C4B and LigB.
the binding of C4BP and Lig proteins is mediated by CCPs 7 and 7 of C4BP with the Big domains 7 and/or 8 of Lig proteins.
The main takeaway from our work is that
C4BP and FH are not only important in the pathogenesis of leptospirosis but also in the pathogenesis and virulence of other spirochetes such as Borrelia burgdorferi and Treponema pallidum.
C4BP and FH are not the sole host proteins involved in the evasion of complement attack by pathogenic leptospires.
the binding of C4BP to LigA and LigA is not sufficient to protect leptospires from complement activation.
